PLE Overview

The Physician Licensure Examination (PLE), also known as the Philippine Medical Boards, is the professional licensure examination required to practise medicine in the Philippines. It is administered twice a year (March and September/October) by the Professional Regulation Commission through the Board of Medicine.

The exam spans 12 subjects across four days over two weekends. Days 1-2 cover six Basic Sciences (Anatomy & Histology, Physiology, Biochemistry, Microbiology & Parasitology, Pathology, and Legal Medicine & Medical Jurisprudence). Days 3-4 cover six Clinical Sciences (Pharmacology, Surgery + ENT & Ophthalmology, Internal Medicine, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Pediatrics & Nutrition, and Preventive Medicine & Public Health). Each subject contains 100 multiple-choice questions and contributes 8.3% to your final grade.

To pass, you need a general average of at least 75% with no individual subject grade below 50%. Failing three times triggers a mandatory refresher course before further attempts.

PLE Details

FormatMultiple-choice questions across 12 subjects
Questions1,200 questions total (100 per subject × 12)
DurationFour exam days across two consecutive weekends
BlueprintPRC Table of Specifications (Basic + Clinical Sciences)
DeliveryPRC testing centers (Manila, Cebu, Davao, Iloilo, Legazpi, others)
Pass mark75% general average, no subject below 50%
SessionsTwice yearly (March + September/October)
AttemptsThree failures require a refresher course before reapplying
Official source: prc.gov.ph ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree from a CHED-recognised medical school in the Philippines.
  • Completion of a 12-month clinical internship at an APMC-accredited training hospital.
  • PRC LERIS account with PSA Birth Certificate and supporting documents uploaded.
  • Examination fees paid through PRC LERIS (~PHP 900 for application; varies per cycle).
  • For IMGs: CHED Certificate of Equivalency plus proof of reciprocity (where applicable).
